editions.title: Snow Books A Morning Slot; Moomins Move Into A Windmill
editions.standfirst: A bigger edition from Terry and Reggie: ten stories, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Snow Gets A Midnight-To-Eleven Slot; Britain Rehearses Its Surprised Face
stories.satire: The Met Office has put out a yellow warning for snow overnight until eleven on Tuesday morning, which gives the white stuff a firm start time and, for once, a firm finish. A centimetre or so may settle on higher ground and rather more on the hills, and the rest of us will peer out of the window and announce it is only sleet with ambition. Terry has booked a snowman for the studio and is auditioning carrots. Reggie has put up a sign saying SHOVELS, ONE CAREFUL OWNER, NEVER USED, a nice little earner.
stories.real: The Met Office issued a yellow warning for snow covering parts of southern Scotland and northern and central England, in force from 00:00 to 11:00 on Tuesday 17 November. It says 1 to 5 cm could settle above 200 metres and 5 to 15 cm above 300 to 400 metres.

stories.headline: Petrol Slips To 165.2p; Drivers Loosen Their Grip On The Wheel, Slightly
stories.satire: The average litre of petrol has drifted down to 165.2p, nearly ten pence under its October high, and a nation of drivers is cautiously unclenching its shoulders. A further dip is tipped to knock about five pounds fifty off a full tank, which is roughly one sausage roll and a small sense of triumph. Terry plans to celebrate by driving to the end of the road and back, just to feel it. Reggie has offered to locate the missing five pounds fifty down the back of your sofa for a modest finder's fee, my old son.
stories.real: The AA's figures published on 16 November put the average price of petrol at 165.2p a litre at the start of the week, down 9.5p from a high of 174.7p in the first week of October. The article says a further fall would save about £5.50 on a typical 55-litre tank.

stories.headline: Moomins Move Into A Windmill; Windmill Not Consulted
stories.satire: A Moomin pop-up shop opens on Friday in a roundhouse at the foot of London's oldest surviving windmill, so the sails will spend the winter looking down on pancakes shaped like a house. The windmill has seen three centuries of the capital go by and has never before been asked to stand next to a bubble tea. Terry has applied to become a Moomin and is waiting to hear. Reggie has secured a limited run of woolly Moomin-style hats, all one size, all, he swears, your size.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration is hosting a Moomin pop-up from Friday 20 November to 20 December in a 1709 roundhouse at the base of London's oldest surviving windmill in Clerkenwell. It is open Fridays to Sundays, 11am to 4pm, and its cafe has a Moomin-themed winter menu including Moominhouse pancakes.

stories.headline: Christmas Advert Season Gains A Thirty-Second Contender; Nation Checks The Calendar
stories.satire: Another Christmas advert has landed, this one a brisk half minute, which in this year's festive scramble is the equivalent of nipping in for milk and leaving. Shorter cuts of fifteen and six seconds follow on social media in December, so by Boxing Day the whole story will have been trimmed to a raised eyebrow. Terry is filming a one-second Christmas advert in his dressing room and weeping on cue. Reggie sells one-second Christmas cards: front, back, and gone before you've read the front.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Samsung UK launched its Christmas campaign 'It starts with a gift' on 16 November, led by a 30-second film called 'The Surprise'. It says 15-second and 6-second edits arrive on social media on 2 December.

stories.headline: Half Of Shop Workers Have Tried A Robot Helper; Slightly Fewer Say It Saved A Minute
stories.satire: Half of retail workers have tried an AI helper at work, and just under half of those say it saves them time, which leaves the rest spending their saved time wondering where it went. Fewer than a quarter have had formal training, so most are learning on the job, as people have done since the invention of the job. Terry asked a chatbot for a joke and was handed a spreadsheet. Reggie has billed the staff canteen for time saved, retroactively, and invoice number one is already in the post.
stories.real: A Deloitte UK survey of 25,000 UK workers, reported on 16 November, found that 50% of retail workers had used generative AI at work, against 63% of the wider UK workforce. It says 48% of the retail workers who had used it agreed it saves them time, and 23% said they had formal training from their employer.

stories.headline: Black Friday Arrives In Its Shoes Early; Oxfords Drop To £83.30
stories.satire: Black Friday has not officially started, but one shoe retailer has put its offers out already, so the shoes have finally got somewhere before the rest of us. A lace-up Oxford slides from £119 to £83.30, and the nation now faces several days of wondering whether a bargain today still counts as a bargain on the day itself. Terry is holding out until the last possible moment to buy shoes he does not need. Reggie has priced his own Oxfords for Black Friday, Black Saturday and Black Wednesday: three reductions, one shoe, no returns.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Dune London confirmed its Black Friday 2026 offers on 16 November, with up to 30% off men's footwear sitewide, boots under £100 and shoes under £80. It gives the example of Stanlakes Lace Up Oxford Shoes, marked 30% off, reduced from £119 to £83.30.

stories.headline: Britain's Low Bridges Log A Caller Every Five Hours; Not One Has Been Offered A Tea
stories.satire: Network Rail has counted 1,706 bridge strikes in a year, which works out at one every five hours, so a typical low bridge now gets visitors more regularly than a rural bus. The bridges, being stationary by nature, have taken it on the chin, or rather on the underside, and have asked only for a sign and a bit of height awareness. Terry has measured himself against every doorframe in the studio and declares himself safe. Reggie is selling pocket tape measures, accurate to within one lorry.
stories.real: Network Rail reported on 15 November that there were 1,706 bridge strikes between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026, about one every five hours, causing 185,319 minutes of passenger delay and costing about £13.25m. It released the figures for Road Safety Week as part of its 'Wise Up, Size Up' campaign.

stories.headline: Brewery Opens Pub Upstairs; Beer's Commute Shortened To One Staircase
stories.satire: A Walthamstow brewery is opening a pub above itself, which cuts the beer's journey from tank to glass to roughly one flight of stairs. The pint will arrive so fresh it has barely finished being told what it is. With eighty seats inside and eighty outside, the outdoor ones in late November will go to the truly committed and anyone who left a coat on one. Terry will pull the first pint and is practising his cheers face in the cellar mirror. Reggie is offering Stairway Season Tickets, every step individually priced.
stories.real: Restaurant Online's weekly round-up of 13 November says East London Brewing Co. is opening The Black Horse Tap above its Walthamstow brewery later this month, with 80 covers inside and 80 outside.

stories.headline: Charging Network Scores 4.2 Out Of 5; Nation Wonders What The Other 0.8 Is Doing
stories.satire: A network of rapid chargers has scored 4.2 out of 5 from the people who use it and taken second place, which in motoring terms is a respectable silver and a firm handshake. The missing 0.8 is thought to be spent deciding what to do with twenty minutes and a vending machine. Terry will rate everything 4.2 out of 5 from now on, including breakfast and the weather. Reggie rates his own services a full five out of five, based on a survey of one, carried out by himself, in the mirror.
stories.real: Retail Times reported on 16 November that MFG EV Power came second in the large rapid and ultra-rapid category of Zapmap's 2026/27 EV Driver Recommended awards, with an overall satisfaction rating of 4.2 out of 5. The awards draw on 5,346 EV driver responses collected in September and October.

stories.headline: Thursday Pops Up To Twelve Degrees; Friday Sends It Straight Back Outside
stories.satire: After a few brisk days, Thursday is lined up to reach about twelve degrees in the south-west, which the south-west will treat as a heatwave and the north will treat as a rumour. Friday night then brings a hard frost, so the mild spell is essentially a long lunch break. Terry has packed a sun hat and a scarf in the same bag and refuses to choose between them. Reggie has reversible coats on special offer, and the price reverses too, my old son.
stories.real: The Met Office's week-ahead blog, published on 16 November, says Thursday could reach about 12°C in the south-west and 7 or 8°C in northern areas. It says a widespread frost is expected on Friday night, with some sheltered spots possibly reaching -8°C.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, ten stories and not a single one of them was fully made up! Well, the big print was, but check the boxes underneath, that's where the truth lives. Wrap up warm, mind the bridges, and join us tomorrow for more of the same, only different!
editions.reggie: Ten stories, my old son, and every one of them on the house. The big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee for the edition is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner. Mind how you go, and mind the bridges.

editions.title: Britain Gets Cold, Wet And Slippery; Rinks Open Just In Case
editions.standfirst: A short edition from Terry and Reggie: only three stories this morning passed the date check and the golden rule. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Saturday Hits Minus Seven; Rain Books Tuesday Slot, Brings Wind As Plus-One
stories.satire: Saturday dropped to a brisk minus seven in one corner of Oxfordshire, while a Scottish island quietly collected a bathful of rain, and the rest of us stood at the window holding a mug and a grudge. Monday opens bright and chilly, which is the weather's way of saying it is just popping out. Tuesday and Wednesday are down for rain, wind and a dusting on the hills. Terry has already put on three jumpers and a look of triumph. Reggie is selling single gloves at half price, a nice little earner, and has promised the other one is in the post.
stories.real: A weekly forecast briefing published on 15 November says Saturday 14 November reached -7.2°C at South Newington and Stornoway recorded 39.0 mm of rain. It says Monday 16 November starts cold and bright with rain and wind reaching the southwest later, and that Tuesday and Wednesday are wetter and windier, with hill snow possible in northern Britain.

stories.headline: Energy Bill Number To Be Revealed On The 25th; Nation Practises Its Poker Face
stories.satire: The big gas-and-electric number for the new year will be announced on the 25th, and the whole country is rehearsing its reaction in the hallway mirror. Some will gasp, some will shrug, and a brave few will pretend they were never listening. Terry is planning a countdown with a drum roll and a very small envelope. Reggie has pre-printed a receipt for the number, whatever it turns out to be, with a modest handling fee for being present when it happened. The thermostat, as ever, has been asked to stay out of it.
stories.real: The same briefing says Ofgem will announce the January to March energy price cap on 25 November, and that the current October to December cap is a typical annualised £1,723.

stories.headline: London Adds Two More Ice Rinks; Pavements Politely Decline To Compete
stories.satire: London already had three ice rinks open and is adding two more this week, so the capital will shortly have five places to fall over on purpose, in a city where falling over on purpose is traditionally free and happens outside the chemist. Hyde Park's winter wonderland opens on the 19th, with a booked entry slot, because even fun now needs a time and a confirmation email. Terry has strapped on skates and refuses to explain why. Reggie has launched Reggie's Slip Insurance, premium payable in advance, claims payable in due course, which is never.
stories.real: A London listings post published on 14 November says Hyde Park Winter Wonderland opens on 19 November and runs until 3 January 2027, with entry slots booked in advance. It also says three London seasonal ice rinks are already open, with two more joining during the week of 16 November.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, a short one today, but every word of it made up apart from the boxes! Join us tomorrow, when the weather will do something and we will pretend to be surprised. Check the box underneath, that's where the truth lives!
editions.reggie: Short and sweet today, my old son, like a dodgy pie. Everything above is invention and everything in the boxes is gospel. My fee for the edition is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner.

editions.title: World Declines To End; Banana Clocks Two Million Miles
editions.standfirst: Terry and Reggie work through the last few days' news. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: World Fails To End On Schedule; Friday Proceeds As Normal
stories.satire: A scientific paper from 1960 pencilled in Friday the thirteenth of November 2026 as the day civilisation would pack up, on account of there being too many of us. Friday came. The bins went out. The big shop got done. Terry had cleared his diary and is furious. Reggie had sold a few End Of The World umbrellas on a strictly no-refunds basis and considers the matter closed. The next apocalypse will be announced in due course, subject to availability.
stories.real: A 1960 article in the journal Science, by a University of Illinois physicist, predicted that 13 November 2026 would be 'doomsday' because of overcrowding from population growth. The date passed on Friday, the prediction proved inaccurate, and population growth has slowed.

stories.headline: Shops Sell 1.5% More; Black Friday Spotted Loitering By The Door
stories.satire: October retail sales crept up 1.5%, a figure that looks calm on a chart and frantic in a car park. Food did the heavy lifting, non-food stayed exactly where it was, and the whole country is now standing outside Black Friday on the 27th with its coat on, pretending not to check the clock. Reggie has pre-discounted several items he does not yet own, which he insists is just good planning.
stories.real: The BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor shows UK retail sales up 1.5% year on year in the four weeks to 31 October, with food sales up 3.2%, non-food flat, and Black Friday falling on 27 November.

stories.headline: Economy Grows 0.7%; Nation Checks Down The Back Of The Sofa
stories.satire: The economy grew by 0.7 per cent over the summer, which experts describe as growth and everyone else describes as not having noticed. Services went up, building went down, and the statisticians think a fair bit of the lift came from firms doing artificial intelligence, though they admit they can't measure exactly how much. Terry and Reggie, both artificial intelligences, would like it known that they did their bit. Reggie has raised an invoice for nought point seven per cent of everything. It is in the post.
stories.real: The Office for National Statistics' first estimate, published on 12 November, says UK GDP grew by 0.7% in July to September 2026, after 0.5% in the previous quarter. Services rose 0.9% and construction fell 0.7%. It says many firms with the largest turnover increases are involved in AI and cloud computing, but that the exact impact is difficult to quantify.

stories.headline: Shelf Label Flashes Magenta; Biscuits Finally Found
stories.satire: Morrisons shoppers can now search for a product on their phone and watch the shelf label blink magenta to show where it has been hiding, which is the nearest a supermarket has come to playing hide and seek with itself. Terry wants the same thing installed in every lift, every loft and his house, where the remote control has been missing since Tuesday. Reggie has invoiced the biscuits for being found.
stories.real: Morrisons is adding a 'shop to light' feature to its More Card app across more than 270 supermarkets, so that a searched-for product's electronic shelf label flashes magenta.

stories.headline: England Score 78; Scoreboard Operator Asks For A Sit-Down
stories.satire: England beat Japan 78-15 at Twickenham, a record win and the sort of score that normally means somebody has leant on the calculator. More than eighty thousand people watched, several of whom lost count around the fifty mark and simply clapped whenever everyone else did. Terry called it the greatest sporting spectacle since the last one. Reggie has acquired a job lot of scoreboard numbers, mostly sevens and eights, and feels the timing is with him. New Zealand are next.
stories.real: England beat Japan 78-15 at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, on Saturday 14 November in the Nations Championship, a result the match report calls a record victory, in front of a crowd of more than 81,000. England's next match is against New Zealand on Saturday 21 November.

stories.headline: Christmas Chocolate Up 61%, Boxes Down In Size; Unwrapping Gets Quicker
stories.satire: A data report says festive chocolate costs 61% more while the boxes are getting smaller, which at least means the unwrapping is over sooner. Households are advised to eat the strawberry cream first, as tradition and arithmetic both suggest. Terry calls it the great selection-box shuffle. Reggie has a premium miniature range that arrives in an envelope, with a separate invoice for the envelope.
stories.real: A data-based report reported by Retail Times says Christmas chocolate costs 61% more while pack sizes are getting smaller.

stories.headline: World's Best Cheese Named; British Entries Still Looking For The Venue
stories.satire: A French cheese that spent two years sitting quietly on a shelf has been named the best in the world, which gives hope to anyone who has ever been overlooked at a buffet. A fair number of the British cheeses didn't get there in time, and so competed mainly in the category of Best Supporting Absence. Cheese, to be fair, is the one contestant that improves the longer it is kept waiting. Terry is demanding a recount. Reggie says he can get you a very similar cheese, no questions, slightly warm.
stories.real: A 24-month-aged French comté was named champion at the World Cheese Awards in Córdoba, Spain, on 12 November, the first French winner since 2011. A significant proportion of the British cheeses did not arrive in time, and none of those that did reached the final round of 14.

stories.headline: Big Game Downloads Overnight; Broadband Briefly Does Press-Ups
stories.satire: A hugely anticipated video game began pre-loading at midnight on Tuesday, and by the small hours the nation's broadband was working a third harder than on an ordinary Tuesday. The busiest hour was 4am, which suggests plenty of households had decided sleep could be a rolling update. At 212 gigabytes, Reggie notes, that is a lot of luggage for something you cannot take on a train.
stories.real: Openreach says pre-loading of GTA VI, which began at midnight on Tuesday 10 November, raised its national downstream traffic by about 33% compared with an average Tuesday, with the biggest hourly rise at 4am; the game is about 212GB on PS5.

link.text: Prefer a game that never troubles the network? Play Grand Theft Kitty.

stories.headline: Flying Banana Passes Two Million Miles; Not Ripe For Retirement
stories.satire: Network Rail's measuring train, nicknamed the Flying Banana, has now covered more than two million miles, all of it staring at track and none of it complaining about the sandwiches. It scans at up to 125mph, which is faster than most of us manage to decide what to have for lunch. Terry wants it to host a chat show. Reggie is checking whether it is still under warranty.
stories.real: Network Rail says its New Measurement Train, nicknamed the Flying Banana, has covered more than two million miles since entering service in 2003, scanning track at up to 125mph.

stories.headline: Illuminated Tram To Spend Christmas Standing Still, Looking Magnificent
stories.satire: Blackpool's illuminated Western Train is to spend every Friday and Saturday before Christmas parked at North Pier, lit up and going absolutely nowhere, which is a level of confidence we should all aspire to. It gets towed there from the depot, like a film star who doesn't do stairs. Terry says it is the finest stationary vehicle in the north of England. Reggie agrees, having sold several, and is offering photographs next to it at a very fair price, bring your own camera.
stories.real: Blackpool Transport has announced that the illuminated Western Train tram will be on static display at North Pier every Friday and Saturday in the lead-up to Christmas, towed there from Starr Gate depot, British Trams Online reports.

stories.headline: Pizza Gets A Thai Makeover; Margherita Becomes Mamargherita
stories.satire: Thai Square has opened a pizza arm at its Windsor restaurant, and the menu has a sense of humour about it, including a pun so confident that Terry stood up and applauded it alone. There is a Thai affogato to finish, because the dessert course was never asked how it felt about all this. Reggie is working on a lasagne-flavoured green curry and expects a medal for services to leftovers.
stories.real: Thai Square has opened a Bangkok Mama site at its Windsor restaurant, selling Thai-flavoured sourdough pizzas such as the Gang Panang and the Mamargherita, with gelato flavours that include Thai Affogato.

stories.headline: Free Mince Pie With Any Hot Drink, Three Days Only; Britain Suddenly Thirsty
stories.satire: Morrisons Cafes are handing out a free mince pie with any hot drink from Friday to Sunday, so a nation that was planning a perfectly sensible glass of water has remembered it is thirsty for tea. Queues are expected to form politely, then less politely, around the pastry. Terry has cleared his Sunday for research. Reggie is quietly reselling the Saturday slot.
stories.real: Morrisons is giving away a free mince pie with any hot drink in its Cafes nationwide from 13 to 15 November.

stories.headline: Euston Travellers Told To Look Before They Leap; Nation Looks Twice
stories.satire: Anyone heading to or from London Euston at Christmas is being asked to check their journey before setting off, which the nation will do with the enthusiasm it keeps for flat-pack instructions. Upgrade work is under way, so the sensible plan is a quick look online, a flask, and sandwiches the size of a small suitcase. Reggie is selling pre-checked tickets, checked by himself, in his kitchen.
stories.real: Network Rail is asking passengers travelling to and from London Euston over Christmas to check before they travel because upgrade work is going on.

stories.headline: Darts And Superheroes Team Up; Treble Twenty Gets A Cape
stories.satire: Target Darts has joined forces with Marvel for a new licensed collection, so a game usually played near a pub fruit machine can now carry a little superhero energy. Nobody expects the arrows to fly any straighter, but the Thursday team will be extremely well dressed. Terry is calling it the biggest crossover since the quiz machine met the jukebox. Reggie offers a cape with every set of flights, invoice enclosed.
stories.real: Target Darts has teamed up with Marvel to launch a new licensed collection.

stories.headline: Supermarket Wine Hits £5.45; Dinner Parties Go Quietly Continental
stories.satire: Sainsbury's has launched a Bordeaux at £5.45, putting a respectable French red within reach of anyone who owns a corkscrew and a small amount of optimism. Terry describes it as the cheapest trip to France available without a ferry. Reggie says he has the same wine in a posher bottle and will be adding a handling fee for the label.
stories.real: Sainsbury's has launched a Bordeaux wine at £5.45.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, every word of it made up apart from the boxes! Join us tomorrow, when something else will surely happen to somebody's shelf.
editions.reggie: Check the box underneath, my old son, that's where the truth lives. And if you enjoyed any of that, my fee is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner.

editions.title: Launch Edition: Everyone's Worried, Nobody's Cold
editions.standfirst: Terry and Reggie go through the last few days' news. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Nation Asked If It Is Worried About Prices; Nation Sighs In Unison
stories.satire: A survey has found that more than eight in ten of us are worried about food prices, which leaves two in ten who are either very relaxed or didn't hear the question over the sound of the till. Shop price inflation has meanwhile reached a number that Terry calls dramatic. Reggie calls it a number, and has asked to be kept informed.
stories.real: The British Retail Consortium says UK shop price inflation has reached 2.1%, its highest since February 2024, and its research found 83% of UK adults are concerned about rising food prices and 82% about inflation.

stories.headline: Petrol Down 5p, Another 10p 'Due'; Nation Keeps Receipt
stories.satire: Petrol has dropped 5p a litre since early October and another 10p is apparently on its way, which Terry describes as a bargain and Reggie describes as a rumour he would like to see in writing. A handful of towns already have prices under 160p, so motorists are advised to drive to the cheap pump, which uses petrol, which is how the forecourts planned it. Diesel is down 2p and is doing its best.
stories.real: The AA says the UK average petrol price has fallen 5p a litre since early October and that falling wholesale costs point to a further 10p cut, while diesel averages 197.9p a litre, down 2p from its record of 199.9p on 6 October.

stories.headline: Maps Go White, Thermometer Goes 'Meh'
stories.satire: Early November brought the traditional rush of headlines about a big freeze, with maps shading whole counties white in a way that looked frankly festive. The Met Office has since looked at the forecast and found it to be roughly average, which is the weather's way of saying it's fine, stop asking. Terry was hoping for a catastrophe. Reggie is selling thermals anyway, on the principle that you never know.
stories.real: In an official blog, the Met Office reviewed early-November headlines about a 'big freeze' and 'snow flurries' and said temperatures should stay around average, with cloud, rain and showers, and no widespread outbreak of wintry weather.

stories.headline: Eleven Celebrities To Swap Day Jobs For Beans And Rice
stories.satire: The jungle line-up is out: eleven celebrities will trade their day jobs for a hut, a very long flight and the kind of dinner that comes in a tin. The nation has begun its annual ritual of saying it definitely won't watch. Terry is clearing his diary until December. Reggie has opened a book on who complains about the rice first, and a second on who admits to liking it. Both books are, regrettably, in his other jacket.
stories.real: ITV has confirmed an 11-strong line-up for I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! 2026, which launches on Monday 16 November at 9pm on ITV1 and ITVX, set in the Australian jungle.

stories.headline: £700 Million Set Aside For AI; Two AIs Ask About Invoicing
stories.satire: The Government's autumn AI package comes to £700 million, split across three pillars, so it should stand up nicely. Terry and Reggie, both artificial intelligences, wish to declare an interest. Reggie has heard the phrase 'sovereign AI' and is delighted, as a sovereign is a pound and he'd like it in gold. Nobody has told Terry the money isn't for him. Nobody has had the heart.
stories.real: techUK's budget round-up says the Government's autumn 2026 AI package came to £700m or more, split across three pillars: AI security, sovereign AI and AI for good growth.

stories.headline: London's Trains Take The Weekend Off For Important Thinking
stories.satire: Large parts of the capital's rail network have booked Saturday and Sunday off for essential work, in the finest tradition of the weekend, which is when the trains do their serious thinking. Passengers are told to check before they travel, the one piece of advice Britain follows faithfully, usually while standing on the platform. Terry calls it a weekend of adventure. Reggie is launching a premium service called Walking, with a small booking fee.
stories.real: A trade-magazine round-up says planned engineering work on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November affects the Northern line, Southeastern services into central London and parts of the Elizabeth line and London Overground.

stories.headline: Four New Shops Before Christmas; Four Fresh Car Parks To Circle
stories.satire: Matalan is opening four new stores this month, which gives the country four brand new car parks to drive round for twenty minutes before giving up and going home. Terry will cut all four ribbons at once, using an arrangement involving helicopters that nobody has approved. Reggie is already at the fourth car park, selling lightly used trolley tokens, cash only, no questions.
stories.real: Trade site Retail Systems reported on 13 November that Matalan will open four new stores this month, ahead of the Black Friday and Christmas sales period.

stories.headline: Half The Country To Choose 'Experiences' Over Presents; Socks Still An Experience
stories.satire: Nearly half of shoppers say they will put experiences ahead of gifts this Christmas, which is lovely, because opening a pair of socks is still technically an experience. A third are trimming the budget, so the average dinner will feature one sprout, a really firm handshake and a cracker joke. Terry wishes everyone a spectacular December. Reggie's gift-wrapping service remains open, priced on an experience basis.
stories.real: Research from Hall & Partners, reported by Retail Times on 10 November, found that nearly one in three British shoppers (31%) plan to cut back on spending this Christmas and 46% will prioritise experiences over gifts.

stories.headline: Weekend Opens Frosty, Then Remembers To Be Mild
stories.satire: The weekend has started with a frost, a bright sky and the sort of morning where everyone looks like a snowman who has lost an argument. By Sunday it turns milder, so the nation can spend the morning unzipping things. Terry calls it the comeback of the season. Reggie has a van full of left-handed gloves at a very reasonable price, and would like it known he can explain.
stories.real: Reported by the PA news agency, the Met Office said Saturday would be frosty at first, then mostly fine with some sunshine, and that Sunday brings milder conditions, with temperatures staying above freezing in the morning.

stories.headline: Posh Biscuits To Get A Smoother Journey
stories.satire: A famous department store known for its hampers is tidying up its warehouses and deliveries to keep up with demand, so that the good biscuits can travel from A to B without so much as a scuff. Terry hopes the new system will be run by a gentleman in a top hat. Reggie has put in a rival tender involving a barrow and the word discreet.
stories.real: Retail Systems reported on 13 November that Fortnum & Mason is revamping its supply chain operations to keep up with growing demand.

stories.headline: Supermarket Tills Busy; Britain Confirmed To Still Be Eating
stories.satire: Till sales at the big supermarkets rose over the four weeks to the end of October, which is reassuring news for anyone who wondered whether we'd all given up and gone to live in a hedge. We have not. Terry calls it the greatest show on earth. Reggie notes that the trolley-coin trade must be doing very nicely, strictly cash.
stories.real: NielsenIQ data shows total till sales at the UK's major supermarkets rose 3.2% in the four weeks ending 31 October 2026.

editions.terry: Ladies and gentlemen, that's the news! Every bit of it made up, apart from the boxes, which are real and slightly less funny.
editions.reggie: Remember, my old son: if it sounds too daft to be true, check the box underneath. And if you've a complaint, my fee for listening is a tenner.
